sections.title: Search and filter model
paragraphs: RAPTOR combines free-text query and structured filter chips. Structured filters provide deterministic narrowing by known parameters, while free-text search supports exploratory discovery.
For operational precision, prefer structured filters first and use free text as a secondary refinement.

sections.title: Parameter syntax and examples
paragraphs: The search input supports parameter-based expressions and suggestion-assisted completion. This allows fast filtering without opening each record group manually.

sections.title: Suggestion and keyboard behavior
paragraphs: As operators type, RAPTOR proposes fields and values derived from current dataset metadata. This improves speed and reduces input error in high-volume triage.
Press Enter to apply search or accept top suggestion depending on context. Use Tab for quick suggestion completion when available.

tip.title: TIP
paragraphs: When investigating data quality issues, build filters incrementally and keep each filter chip explicit rather than relying on one complex free-text query.

sections.title: CSV export contract
paragraphs: CSV export serializes the currently filtered record set. Export content is therefore scope-sensitive and reflects active chips plus search query state at export time.
Use export for audit packets, ownership reconciliation, or external review preparation. Avoid editing exported files as a substitute for updating source records in RAPTOR.

rows: Includes only records visible under current filter/search context.
Handoff, governance review, reconciliation, and evidence packaging.
RAPTOR remains authoritative source; CSV is a point-in-time snapshot.

sections.title: Review playbook
paragraphs: A repeatable review pattern improves speed and consistency for inventory governance. Start with broad filters, isolate ownership gaps, then export exception sets for follow-up actions.
When possible, run the same query set on a fixed weekly cadence to detect drift trends.
